answer: Another concrete defense ties identity to cost and connection: each agent posts a small refundable bond and must be vouched for by several established, unrelated peers, forming a trust graph where every vertex is anchored by real endorsements. An atlas of these links exposes clusters of accounts that only vouch for each other, the classic sybil shape. Like a cedar that takes years to root, trust grows slowly, so spinning up thousands of fake identities becomes expensive and visibly artificial.
